title: Adiabatic Coupler With Design-Intended Splitting Ratio (Mao et al., J. Lightwave Technol. 37(24), 2019)
figure: Fig. 1, page 2 (journal p. 6148) — general ADC schematic with labelled design parameters
dims_source: Section II-B six-step segmented optimization, pp. 6150-6152: w = 350 nm and g2 = 150 nm chosen beforehand (p. 6150); g1 = 3 um from crosstalk convergence, Fig. 5 (p. 6150); (w1, w2) = (400 nm, 300 nm) and Ls1 = 20 um chosen over (425, 275) for Region III area (p. 6150); Lt = 5 um, Fig. 7 (p. 6150); Ls2 = 10 um, Fig. 8 (p. 6151); L = 200 um from IL_III convergence at L >= 180 um, Fig. 9 (p. 6152); w3 = 350 nm, w4 = w3 - dw_out with dw_out = 0..50 nm setting the splitting ratio (pp. 6149, 6151)
notes: device_bw.png is a clean redraw of the Fig. 1 topology at the paper's stated dimensions, not a figure crop (the paper's schematic has labels baked in and is itself not to scale). Five regions: input tapers (Lt, w->w1/w2, gap g1 constant), input S-bends (Ls1, gap g1->g2), adiabatic coupling tapers (L, gap g2 constant, w1->w3 upper / w2->w4 lower), output S-bends (Ls2, gap g2->g1), output tapers (Lt, ->w). Inner edges hold the stated gaps; widths taper on the outer edges. Drawn variant: dw_out = 0 (50/50 3-dB device, the paper's thermal-stability demo); the 0-50 nm dw_out knob is sub-pixel and is the retarget spec knob, not a drawable feature. Rendering exaggerates the transverse axis (~16x; image 2400x600 over 240 x 3.9 um window) for legibility, matching the final1 fixture convention and the paper's own not-to-scale schematic; x-axis proportions are true (coupling region = 200/240 of length). O-band device (1260-1360 nm, center 1310 nm), SOI 220 nm strip, TE.
